title: Microsoft Teams: choose the institution type in the Teams for Education Policy Wizard
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap details, institution-type choices, licensing and policy-assignment behaviour are supported. Minor corrections should complete the wizard paths, acknowledge Microsoft's separate warning about new event policies, and remove a policy-check instruction not represented in the controls table.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The wizard adjusts students' Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions according to institution type.
claims.quote: Students: The wizard adjusts the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition of each policy area covered by the wizard with new default settings that are appropriate to keep your students safe.

claims.claim: The wizard creates custom policy definitions for educators and staff for each policy area it covers.
claims.quote: Educators and staff: The wizard creates a set of custom policy definitions for each policy area covered by the wizard with settings tailored to the needs of educators and staff.

claims.claim: The custom educator and staff policies are assigned to groups the administrator selects.
claims.quote: Then, it assigns the policy definitions to the group of educators and staff that you choose.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The wizard accepts up to three educator and staff groups.
claims.quote: You can select up to three groups.

claims.claim: Learn lists seven student policy areas: Teams, Meeting, Live events, App setup, App permission, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote: Students ... Teams policy ... Meeting policy ... Live events policy ... App setup policy ... App permission policy ... Messaging policy ... Calling policy

claims.claim: Learn lists five educator and staff custom policy areas: Teams, Meeting, Live events, Messaging and Calling.
claims.quote: Educators and staff ... Teams policy ... Meeting policy ... Live events policy ... Messaging policy ... Calling policy

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Changing only the institution type applies student Global policy definitions based on the new type.
claims.quote: Change only the educational institution type ... Students: The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions based on the new educational institution type are applied to students.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change; After rollout
claims.claim: Changing only the type creates and assigns new educator and staff definitions, removing the previous type's definitions from those groups.
claims.quote: A set of custom policy definitions based on the new educational institution type is created and assigned to the educators and staff groups. The custom policy definitions created for the previous educational institution type are removed from the educators and staff groups.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's wizard page says education defaults for new Teams features are added to Global policies automatically without administrator intervention.
claims.quote: whenever a new feature is added to Teams, the appropriate EDU relevant default value of the policy for that feature will be automatically added to the Global (Org-wide default) without requiring any admin intervention.
claims.fix: After the automatic-defaults sentence in Why it matters, add: 'Microsoft's academic-year guidance also warns that webinars and town halls are controlled by a separate policy and need to be disabled for students.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/education/guide/1-reference/teams-microsoft-365-groups#recent-changes-to-teams, which says 'as events (webinars and town halls) are now controlled by a separate policy, they need to be disabled for students as well'.

claims.claim: No source examined says existing policies change if nobody runs the wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Education Policy Wizard institution type default Apply license pricing role; "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" data access license meter role default rollout date. Read roadmap description and easy-policy-setup-edu; application is described as following Apply.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new data access mechanism for institution-type selection.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams for Education Policy Wizard" data access license meter role default rollout date. Read roadmap description and easy-policy-setup-edu in full; they describe policy configuration, not a new data access mechanism.

claims.claim: The wizard's App permission and Messaging policy settings affect which apps and sharing features students can use.
claims.quote: Microsoft apps | Block specific apps and allow all others > Walkie Talkie blocked | Allow all apps ... Chat | Off | On ... Giphys in conversations | Off | On

claims.claim: Learn describes student policies as more restrictive than educator and staff policies.
claims.quote: Policies for students need to be more restrictive to reduce their risk of receiving inappropriate levels of access. Educators and staff need a separate set of policies that can be more permissive

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing direct or group student assignments must be removed for the wizard's Global policy definitions to take effect.
claims.quote: Remove all existing direct assignments and group assignments from your students so that the Global (Org-wide default) policy definition applied by the wizard takes effect.

claims.claim: The wizard assigns educator and staff group policies at ranking 1, the highest ranking.
claims.quote: the wizard assigns policies to your educators and staff group using a group assignment ranking of 1, which is the highest ranking.

claims.claim: An existing policy of the same area assigned to the selected educator and staff group is moved to a lower ranking.
claims.quote: If your educators and staff group has an existing policy of the same policy area assigned to it, that existing policy is moved to a lower ranking and the policy assigned by the wizard takes effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Conflicting direct educator and staff assignments override the wizard's group assignments and must be removed for its custom policies to take effect.
claims.quote: Remove any conflicting direct assignments for your educators and staff so that the custom policy definition created by the wizard takes effect.

claims.claim: The wizard starts automatically for administrators who are new to Teams.
claims.quote: If you're new to Teams, the wizard automatically starts.

claims.claim: The wizard article does not say that merely starting the wizard applies its policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Education Policy Wizard institution type default Apply license pricing role. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full: automatic starting is step 1; applying changes is separately documented at step 5.

claims.claim: Completing Apply may take a few minutes, with student Global policy definitions immediately applied.
claims.quote: Select Apply to apply your changes. This may take a few minutes to complete.The Global (Org-wide default) policy definitions are immediately applied to students.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Custom policy assignment to educator and staff group members can take a few hours depending on group size.
claims.quote: For your educators and staff, it could take a few hours for the custom policies to be assigned to each member of the groups you selected, depending on the size of the groups.

claims.claim: Learn describes no mechanism carrying edits in the previous type's custom policies into the new definitions.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Education Policy Wizard institution type tenant type PowerShell Microsoft Graph configuration. Read easy-policy-setup-edu in full, particularly Make changes in the wizard; it describes new definitions and removal of previous definitions, not migration of edits.

claims.claim: Learn instructs administrators with no educator and staff groups to create a group and rerun the wizard.
claims.quote: If you don't have any groups set up yet for your educators and staff, create a group, and then rerun the wizard.

claims.claim: The wizard provides a review of selections before Apply.
claims.quote: 4. Review your selections. ... 5. Select Apply to apply your changes.

claims.claim: Learn recommends checking Message Center for new Teams features and policy settings.
claims.quote: But do check the Message Center (in the Microsoft 365 admin center) frequently to stay up to date on new features and their policies and policy settings in Teams.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration lists other education configuration parameters but none for institution type.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "institution type" "PowerShell" "wizard". Read the complete Set-CsTeamsEducationConfiguration reference: ParentGuardianPreferredContactMethod, UpdateParentInformation, EduGenerativeAIEnhancements, Identity, WhatIf and Confirm; no institution-type parameter.
